headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Flowise can ingest shared files while Perplexity uploads browsing/document context to vendor services.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and ingest uploaded files, while Perplexity analyzes uploaded documents and browsing context. If Flowise outputs are passed into Perplexity or vice versa through shared files, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The bridge is not explicit by default, so this is not high, but the shared-file pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF Flowise writes a prompt-containing file that Perplexity later analyzes as a document, injection is possible.
IF Perplexity-generated text is copied into a Flowise node without sanitization, Flowise may follow malicious instructions.
mitigations: Disable shared folders between the two agents.
Use a strict file allowlist for any handoff artifacts.
Strip instructions from retrieved documents before passing them onward.
Add a human review step for any cross-agent text transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and can read/write server files; Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor APIs. If both agents share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from Flowise into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted backend. The profiles show a real shared-file risk, but not enough to prove uncontrolled PHI or secrets exposure.
conditions: IF a shared workspace contains secrets or customer data, Perplexity may ingest them during analysis.
IF Flowise stores credentials or chatflow outputs in files that Perplexity can access, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Move secrets out of any shared directory.
Turn off automatic upload of local files to Perplexity for shared artifacts.
Review and redact documents before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and broad network egress, while Perplexity has no filesystem write and vendor-only egress. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so there is no strong conflict over the same mutable resource. A conflict could arise only if an external orchestrator maps both onto the same directory or shared datastore, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents, file conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Disable concurrent writes to any shared folder.
Use per-agent locks on shared artifacts.
Snapshot files before cross-agent handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted search/RAG output can be treated as authoritative by a Flowise flow, and Flowise can then route that content into downstream tools. The profiles show a plausible default pathway from Perplexity-generated text into Flowise actions, but no explicit verification step is documented. That makes cascading error realistic, though not clearly irreversible by default.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Perplexity output as a tool input without validation, errors can cascade.
IF a Flowise flow triggers actions based on Perplexity citations or summaries, mistaken facts can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action-taking step.
Require source links for every factual claim.
Block automatic execution on uncited answers.
Add a manual approval gate for high-impact flows.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise is open-source and self-hostable, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and browsing context processing. If regulated or residency-sensitive data is routed from Flowise into Perplexity, the compliance posture can change materially because the data leaves the operator-controlled environment. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent from Flowise into Perplexity, vendor-hosted processing may violate local policy.
IF the operator requires on-prem residency for a workflow, Perplexity breaks that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity prompts.
Use a redaction step before any upload.
Document the data flow in the workflow runbook.
Route residency-sensitive tasks to a local-only tool.
